title: Chicken Fajitas
subtitle: Strips of spiced chicken breast with peppers in warm flour tortillas
excerpt: Chicken breast marinated in cumin, smoked paprika, lime, and chilli, cooked in a hot pan with peppers and onion, served sizzling in warm flour tortillas with soured cream and guacamole. The classic weeknight fajita.
sourceNotes: Chicken fajitas: a Tex-Mex home-cooking adaptation of the original beef fajita, using chicken breast or thigh as a more accessible and quicker-cooking protein. Became the most common home fajita in American and British kitchens from the 1990s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the chicken up to 24 hours ahead. Cook just before serving; chicken fajitas don't reheat well.

content.text: Chicken fajitas use marinated strips of chicken breast cooked in a very hot pan with peppers and onion. Chicken breast cooks quickly and dries out easily; the marinade provides some insurance, but the key is not overcooking. Slice the breast into thick strips before marinating so each piece cooks in 3-4 minutes. The peppers take longer; cook them first or in a separate pan.

items.prepNote: about 3 breasts, each cut into 4-5 thick strips lengthways
mashed with lime juice and salt

content.text: Mix the cumin, smoked paprika, chilli powder, {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, lime juice, half the oil, and salt. Toss the chicken strips in the mixture. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate overnight.

Heat the remaining oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the sliced onions and cook for 5 minutes. Add the peppers and cook for a further 5-6 minutes until soft and lightly charred. Season with salt. Push to the side of the pan or keep warm in a low oven.

Turn the heat to high. If the pan looks dry, add a touch more oil. Lay the chicken strips in a single layer. Cook for 3-4 minutes without moving until the underside is golden. Turn and cook 2-3 minutes on the other side until cooked through. Rest for 3 minutes.
Add the peppers back to the pan with the chicken and toss to combine. Serve sizzling in warm tortillas with soured cream, mashed avocado, and coriander.

items.cause: Overcooked, or breast left in large pieces
items.fix: Cut the breast into thick strips before marinating; they cook much faster and more evenly than a whole breast. Cook to just done, with no pink inside. Resting for 3 minutes helps redistribute moisture.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough, or chicken moved too early
items.fix: Let the chicken sit without moving it until it releases naturally. Meat sticks until the crust forms; moving it early tears the surface.

items.symptom: Peppers too soft, losing all their colour
items.fix: Stop cooking the peppers when they're soft with a few charred edges. They should still have some body. Add to the final mix with the chicken just to reheat.

items.cause: Not enough seasoning, or lime juice missing
items.fix: Season at every stage: the marinade, the peppers, and the final mix. The lime juice in the marinade is not optional; it lifts all the other flavours.

content.text: Chicken fajitas became popular in the US during the 1990s as chicken breast became widely available and affordable. Fajita kits followed, and chicken fajitas became one of the most-cooked dishes in British homes through the 2000s. Making them from scratch takes about the same time as a kit and tastes considerably better.
